Violet Jessop was on board for three disasters, on three sister ships. And she survived all of them.
In 1911, she was a stewardess on the Olympic, the biggest ship in the world, when it crashed into a warship.
The Olympic limped home. Violet was fine.
A year later, she joined its sister ship. The Titanic.
When it hit the iceberg, she was ordered into a lifeboat, and an officer handed her a baby to look after.
The next morning, on the rescue ship, a woman ran up, grabbed the baby, and left without a word.
Four years later, during World War One, Violet was a nurse on the third sister. The Britannic, now a hospital ship.
It hit a mine, and sank in under an hour.
This time, before she ran, she went back for one thing. Her toothbrush. She had missed it after the Titanic.
Her lifeboat was being pulled into the ship's spinning propellers. So she jumped.
She was dragged under, and hit her head on a boat, but she survived. Years later, a doctor found she had fractured her skull.
And she kept working at sea for decades. They called her Miss Unsinkable.
